- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast increase to 2–3% max for next period.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model often underestimates; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% relative to prior forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early periods of a 30-day forecast (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% upward bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment history shows repeated small positive signals (e.g., 0.20), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast slope slightly.
- If true outcome deviates from model by >5% in first 3–5 days, assume model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent true trend if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, reduce forecast slope or add 1–2% downward bias to prevent overcorrection.
